description: Structured evidence and expected troubleshooting paths for Cisco-style network troubleshooting cases.

scenario.symptom: PC-01 can reach its default gateway but cannot reach Server-01 on another network.

observations.description: PC-01 cannot reach Server-01.

next_command.reason: Determine whether R1 has a route to the destination network.

expected_evidence.interpretation: R1 has no route to the destination network.

diagnosis.explanation: The routing table does not contain a route to the destination network.

recommended_fix.description: Configure or restore the appropriate route according to the intended topology.

verification.expected_result: R1 has a valid route to 192.168.30.0/24 and PC-01 can reach Server-01.

scenario.symptom: PC-01 cannot communicate with other devices on its local network.

observations.description: PC-01 cannot communicate with other devices on its local network.

evidence.description: PC-01 is configured with IP address 192.168.20.20 and gateway 192.168.10.1.

next_command.reason: Verify the endpoint IP address, subnet mask, and default gateway against the intended network.

expected_evidence.interpretation: The PC has an IP address from the wrong network.

diagnosis.explanation: PC-01 is configured with an address from 192.168.20.0/24 even though it is intended to belong to 192.168.10.0/24.

recommended_fix.description: Configure PC-01 with an IP address belonging to the intended network, such as 192.168.10.20.

verification.expected_result: PC-01 has a valid address in 192.168.10.0/24 and can communicate with devices on the local network.

scenario.symptom: PC-01 cannot reliably communicate with devices that should belong to the same network.

observations.description: PC-01 cannot reliably reach devices that should belong to the same network.

evidence.description: PC-01 has IP address 192.168.10.20 with subnet mask 255.255.0.0.

next_command.reason: Verify that the subnet mask matches the intended network design.

expected_evidence.interpretation: The configured subnet mask is broader than the intended /24 network.

diagnosis.explanation: PC-01 uses 255.255.0.0 instead of the intended 255.255.255.0 subnet mask.

recommended_fix.description: Configure PC-01 with subnet mask 255.255.255.0.

verification.expected_result: PC-01 correctly identifies the intended local network and can communicate with the expected devices.

scenario.symptom: PC-01 can communicate with devices on its local subnet but cannot reach devices on other networks.

observations.description: PC-01 can reach local devices but cannot reach remote networks.

evidence.description: PC-01 is configured with default gateway 192.168.20.1 instead of 192.168.10.1.

next_command.reason: Verify that the configured default gateway belongs to the PC's local network and matches the intended gateway.

expected_evidence.interpretation: The configured gateway does not match the intended gateway 192.168.10.1.

diagnosis.explanation: PC-01 uses a gateway outside its intended 192.168.10.0/24 network.

recommended_fix.description: Configure PC-01 to use default gateway 192.168.10.1.

verification.expected_result: PC-01 can reach 192.168.10.1 and then communicate with destinations on remote networks.

scenario.symptom: PC-01 intermittently loses connectivity or communication with another device using the same IP address is inconsistent.

observations.description: Connectivity is intermittent.

next_command.reason: Compare endpoint IP configurations and determine whether the same address is assigned to multiple devices.

expected_evidence.interpretation: PC-02 uses the same IP address.

diagnosis.explanation: PC-01 and PC-02 are configured with the same IPv4 address.

recommended_fix.description: Assign a unique IP address to one of the devices while keeping it within the intended subnet.

verification.expected_result: Each device has a unique IP address and both devices can communicate normally.

scenario.symptom: PC-01 cannot communicate with the network.

observations.description: PC-01 cannot communicate with the network.

next_command.reason: Determine whether the router interface connected to the local network is operational.

expected_evidence.interpretation: The interface has been administratively disabled.

diagnosis.explanation: The affected router interface is administratively disabled.

recommended_fix.description: Enter the affected interface configuration and enable it with no shutdown.

verification.expected_result: The interface reports up/up and PC-01 can reach its default gateway.

scenario.symptom: PC-01 cannot reach the network even though its IP configuration appears correct.

observations.description: PC-01 cannot reach the network.

evidence.description: The interface connected to PC-01 reports down/down.

next_command.reason: Determine whether the switch port connected to the endpoint has an operational link.

expected_evidence.interpretation: The switch port does not have an operational physical link.

diagnosis.explanation: The endpoint-facing switch port has no operational link, indicating a possible cable, port, or physical connectivity problem.

recommended_fix.description: Restore the physical connection or correct the affected port/link configuration.

verification.expected_result: The switch port reports an operational link and PC-01 can communicate with the network.

scenario.symptom: A router interface has an IP address configured, but devices connected through it cannot communicate.

observations.description: The interface has an IP address but reports up/down.

next_command.reason: Separate an interface that is administratively disabled from one whose physical layer is up but protocol is down.

expected_evidence.interpretation: The physical interface is up, but the line protocol is down.

diagnosis.explanation: The interface is physically up but its line protocol is down, indicating an underlying Layer 1 or Layer 2 connectivity problem.

recommended_fix.description: Investigate and restore the underlying link or neighboring interface configuration.

verification.expected_result: The interface reports up/up and connectivity through the interface is restored.

scenario.symptom: PC-01 has a valid IP address and default gateway configured, but it cannot ping its gateway.

observations.description: PC-01 cannot ping 192.168.10.1.

next_command.reason: Verify that the router interface providing the default gateway is operational.

expected_evidence.interpretation: Inspect whether the gateway interface is operational.

diagnosis.explanation: The endpoint has the expected gateway configured but cannot reach it, so the local path between the endpoint and gateway requires investigation.

recommended_fix.description: Correct the local connectivity problem identified during investigation, such as an interface, VLAN, or physical-link issue.

verification.expected_result: PC-01 successfully pings 192.168.10.1 before remote-network connectivity is tested.

scenario.symptom: PC-01 cannot communicate with other devices that should be in the same VLAN.

observations.description: PC-01 cannot communicate with other devices that should be in VLAN 10.

next_command.reason: Determine whether the required VLAN exists and which ports are assigned to it.

expected_evidence.interpretation: The required VLAN does not exist on the switch.

diagnosis.explanation: VLAN 10 is required by the topology but is absent from the switch VLAN table.

recommended_fix.description: Create VLAN 10 and assign the appropriate switch ports according to the intended topology.

verification.expected_result: VLAN 10 exists on SW-01, the endpoint port belongs to VLAN 10, and PC-01 can communicate with the intended VLAN members.

scenario.symptom: PC-01 has a valid IP configuration but cannot communicate with devices in its intended VLAN.

observations.description: PC-01 cannot communicate with devices in its intended VLAN.

evidence.description: PC-01 is connected to Fa0/6, which is assigned to VLAN 20 instead of VLAN 10.

next_command.reason: Identify the VLAN assignment of the switch port connected to PC-01.

expected_evidence.interpretation: The endpoint port belongs to the wrong VLAN.

diagnosis.explanation: The PC's access port is assigned to VLAN 20 even though the endpoint is intended to belong to VLAN 10.

recommended_fix.description: Assign Fa0/6 to VLAN 10 according to the intended network design.

verification.expected_result: Fa0/6 is an access port in VLAN 10 and PC-01 can communicate with the intended VLAN 10 devices.

cases.title: Incorrect Access or Trunk Port Mode

scenario.symptom: Devices across an inter-switch connection cannot communicate across the expected VLAN path.

observations.description: The inter-switch link does not carry the expected VLAN traffic.

evidence.description: The inter-switch interface is operating as an access port.

next_command.reason: Determine whether the inter-switch interface is configured and operating as the intended trunk.

expected_evidence.interpretation: The inter-switch interface is configured as an access port instead of a trunk.

diagnosis.explanation: The inter-switch link is expected to carry multiple VLANs but is operating in access mode.

recommended_fix.description: Configure the inter-switch link as a trunk according to the intended topology.

verification.expected_result: The inter-switch interface operates as a trunk and the required VLAN traffic crosses the link.

scenario.symptom: Two hosts that should be in the same VLAN cannot communicate even though both have valid IP configurations.

observations.description: PC-01 cannot communicate with PC-02 even though both should belong to VLAN 10.

evidence.description: PC-01's access port Fa0/5 belongs to VLAN 10.
PC-02's access port Fa0/5 belongs to VLAN 20.

next_command.reason: Identify the VLAN assignment of the endpoint port and compare it with the intended topology.

expected_evidence.interpretation: PC-01 is assigned to VLAN 10.
PC-02 is assigned to VLAN 20 instead of VLAN 10.

diagnosis.explanation: The endpoint ports are assigned to different VLANs even though both devices are intended to belong to VLAN 10.

recommended_fix.description: Assign both endpoint ports to VLAN 10 according to the intended topology and verify that the inter-switch trunk carries VLAN 10.

verification.expected_result: Both endpoint ports belong to VLAN 10, VLAN 10 is carried between the switches, and PC-01 can communicate with PC-02.

scenario.symptom: Devices in the same VLAN but connected to different switches cannot communicate.

observations.description: PC-01 cannot communicate with PC-02 even though both should belong to VLAN 10.

next_command.reason: Determine whether the inter-switch link is operating as a trunk and whether the expected VLAN is being carried.

expected_evidence.interpretation: The inter-switch interface is not operating as a trunk.

diagnosis.explanation: The inter-switch link expected to carry VLAN 10 is not operating as a trunk.

recommended_fix.description: Configure the inter-switch link according to the intended topology so that it operates as a trunk.

verification.expected_result: The inter-switch link reports trunking and VLAN 10 is carried between SW-01 and SW-02.

scenario.symptom: Devices in VLAN 20 can communicate when connected to the same switch but cannot communicate when separated across two switches.

observations.description: PC-01 cannot communicate with PC-02 across the inter-switch link.

next_command.reason: Check whether VLAN 20 is included in the trunk's allowed VLAN list.

expected_evidence.interpretation: VLAN 20 is missing from the trunk's allowed VLAN list.

diagnosis.explanation: The trunk is operational, but VLAN 20 is filtered because it is not included in the allowed VLAN list.

recommended_fix.description: Allow VLAN 20 on the appropriate trunk according to the intended topology.

verification.expected_result: VLAN 20 appears in the trunk's allowed VLAN list and VLAN 20 endpoints can communicate across the switches.

scenario.symptom: An inter-switch trunk is operational but native-VLAN-related connectivity problems or warnings occur.

observations.description: The inter-switch trunk has a native VLAN mismatch.

next_command.reason: Compare the native VLAN configured on the local trunk with the intended topology and the remote switch.

expected_evidence.interpretation: SW-01 uses native VLAN 99; the remote side must be checked to confirm the native VLAN matches.
SW-02 uses native VLAN 1, creating a native VLAN mismatch.

diagnosis.explanation: The two ends of the trunk use different native VLANs.

recommended_fix.description: Configure the same intended native VLAN on both ends of the trunk.

verification.expected_result: Both ends of the trunk report the same native VLAN and the native-VLAN mismatch is resolved.

scenario.symptom: PC-01 can reach its default gateway but cannot reach Server-01 on another network.

observations.description: PC-01 can reach its default gateway but cannot reach Server-01.

next_command.reason: Determine whether R1 has a route to the destination network.

expected_evidence.interpretation: R1 does not have a route to the destination network.

diagnosis.explanation: The routing table does not contain a route to 192.168.30.0/24.

recommended_fix.description: Configure or restore the appropriate route to 192.168.30.0/24 according to the intended topology.

verification.expected_result: R1 has a valid route to 192.168.30.0/24 and PC-01 can reach Server-01.

scenario.symptom: Traffic reaches R1 but is forwarded along the wrong path toward the destination network.

observations.description: Traffic toward the remote network does not reach Server-01.

next_command.reason: Inspect the route selected by R1 for the destination network.

expected_evidence.interpretation: R1 has a route, but its next hop does not match the intended topology.

diagnosis.explanation: R1 has a route to the destination network, but the route points traffic along an incorrect path.

recommended_fix.description: Correct the routing configuration so traffic uses the intended path to 192.168.30.0/24.

verification.expected_result: R1 selects the intended route and traffic reaches Server-01.

scenario.symptom: Internal networks are reachable, but traffic to unknown or external networks fails.

observations.description: R1 can reach known internal networks but cannot forward traffic toward unknown or external networks.

next_command.reason: Determine whether R1 has a default route for destinations that are not otherwise known.

expected_evidence.interpretation: R1 has no default route.

diagnosis.explanation: R1 has no 0.0.0.0/0 route for forwarding traffic toward unknown networks.

recommended_fix.description: Configure the appropriate default route toward the upstream router according to the intended topology.

verification.expected_result: R1 has a valid default route and can forward traffic toward destinations not present as more specific routes.

scenario.symptom: A route exists for the destination network, but packets do not reach the destination.

observations.description: The destination network is known but is unreachable.

next_command.reason: Inspect the configured next hop for the destination network and compare it with the intended topology.

expected_evidence.interpretation: The configured next hop is 192.168.20.3, while the intended next hop is 192.168.20.2.

diagnosis.explanation: The route to 192.168.30.0/24 points to the wrong next-hop address.

recommended_fix.description: Correct the route so that it uses the intended next-hop address 192.168.20.2.

verification.expected_result: The route points to the correct next hop and traffic reaches the destination network.

scenario.symptom: Traffic toward a destination network does not arrive and repeated routing behavior is observed.

routing.expected_behavior: Traffic should progress toward the destination without returning to the previous router.

observations.description: Traffic repeatedly traverses R1 and R2 instead of progressing toward the destination.

next_command.reason: Determine whether packets repeatedly traverse the same routers instead of progressing toward the destination.

expected_evidence.interpretation: The path repeatedly returns to previously visited routers, indicating a possible routing loop.

diagnosis.explanation: Incorrect routing information causes traffic for the destination to circulate between routers.

recommended_fix.description: Inspect and correct the routing entries on the involved routers so the destination has a valid forward path without returning traffic to the previous router.

verification.expected_result: Traceroute progresses toward the destination without repeated router hops and the destination becomes reachable.

scenario.symptom: Devices in VLAN 10 can communicate with each other, but they cannot communicate with devices in VLAN 20.

observations.description: VLAN 10 hosts can communicate locally but inter-VLAN communication with VLAN 20 fails.

next_command.reason: Determine whether R1 has operational subinterfaces for all required VLANs.

expected_evidence.interpretation: The VLAN 10 subinterface exists.
The required VLAN 20 subinterface is missing.

diagnosis.explanation: R1 does not have the required subinterface for VLAN 20, so it cannot provide Layer 3 gateway functionality for that VLAN.

recommended_fix.description: Create and configure the VLAN 20 router subinterface with the appropriate 802.1Q encapsulation and gateway address.

verification.expected_result: The VLAN 20 subinterface is operational, hosts can reach 192.168.20.1, and inter-VLAN communication succeeds.

scenario.symptom: VLAN 20 hosts cannot communicate through the router even though a router subinterface is configured.

observations.description: VLAN 20 host cannot reach its router gateway.

next_command.reason: Inspect the router subinterface and verify that its 802.1Q VLAN tag matches VLAN 20.

expected_evidence.interpretation: The expected VLAN 20 subinterface exists.
The subinterface is tagged for VLAN 30 instead of VLAN 20.

diagnosis.explanation: The VLAN 20 subinterface uses an 802.1Q tag for VLAN 30, so VLAN 20 traffic is not mapped to the intended Layer 3 interface.

recommended_fix.description: Configure the subinterface with the correct 802.1Q VLAN ID of 20.

verification.expected_result: The subinterface uses VLAN 20 tagging and VLAN 20 hosts can reach their gateway.

cases.title: Trunk Does Not Carry Required VLAN to Router

scenario.symptom: VLAN 10 hosts can reach their gateway, but VLAN 20 hosts cannot reach their gateway.

observations.description: VLAN 10 host can reach 192.168.10.1.
VLAN 20 host cannot reach 192.168.20.1.

next_command.reason: Determine whether VLAN 20 is being carried from the switch to the router.

expected_evidence.interpretation: The trunk allows VLAN 10 but does not allow VLAN 20.

diagnosis.explanation: The switch-to-router trunk does not allow VLAN 20, preventing VLAN 20 traffic from reaching the router subinterface.

recommended_fix.description: Allow VLAN 20 on the switch-to-router trunk according to the intended topology.

verification.expected_result: VLAN 20 is allowed on the trunk, the VLAN 20 host can reach 192.168.20.1, and inter-VLAN routing works.

scenario.symptom: PC-01 does not receive an IP address automatically.

observations.description: PC-01 does not receive an IP address through DHCP.

next_command.reason: Inspect the router configuration to determine whether a DHCP pool exists for the client network.

expected_evidence.interpretation: The router does not have a DHCP pool configured for the client network.

diagnosis.explanation: No DHCP pool exists for the 192.168.10.0/24 client network.

recommended_fix.description: Create the appropriate DHCP pool with the correct network, subnet mask, and default gateway.

verification.expected_result: PC-01 successfully obtains an IP address from the expected DHCP network.

scenario.symptom: PC-01 receives an IP address automatically but cannot communicate with devices outside its local network.

observations.description: PC-01 has an IP address but cannot reach remote networks.

evidence.description: The DHCP-provided default gateway is 192.168.20.1 instead of 192.168.10.1.

next_command.reason: Inspect the DHCP pool and verify that the configured default gateway matches the client network.

expected_evidence.interpretation: The DHCP pool provides a gateway from the wrong network.

diagnosis.explanation: The DHCP pool provides 192.168.20.1 as the gateway even though the clients belong to 192.168.10.0/24 and should use 192.168.10.1.

recommended_fix.description: Configure the DHCP pool to provide the correct default gateway 192.168.10.1.

verification.expected_result: After renewing the DHCP lease, PC-01 receives 192.168.10.1 as its default gateway and can reach remote networks.

scenario.symptom: New clients cannot obtain an IP address through DHCP while existing clients continue to work.

observations.description: PC-03 cannot obtain an IP address while existing clients continue to operate.

next_command.reason: Determine the total and leased DHCP addresses and whether the pool has been exhausted.

expected_evidence.interpretation: All 11 available addresses in the DHCP pool are currently leased.
The DHCP pool has no remaining addresses for new clients.

diagnosis.explanation: All addresses available in the DHCP pool are currently leased, preventing new clients from obtaining an address.

recommended_fix.description: Expand or redesign the DHCP address pool according to the intended network design, or release stale leases where appropriate.

verification.expected_result: A new client can obtain a valid DHCP lease from the available address pool.

scenario.symptom: PC-01 can reach its gateway but cannot reach Server-01.

expected_state.policy: Traffic from 192.168.10.0/24 to 192.168.30.0/24 should be permitted.

observations.description: PC-01 can reach its gateway but cannot reach Server-01.

next_command.reason: Determine whether an ACL is explicitly denying traffic between the client and server networks.

expected_evidence.interpretation: The ACL explicitly denies traffic from the client network to the server network.

diagnosis.explanation: An ACL contains a deny rule that blocks traffic which should be permitted according to the intended policy.

recommended_fix.description: Modify the ACL according to the intended security policy so that legitimate traffic is permitted.

verification.expected_result: The intended traffic is permitted and PC-01 can reach Server-01.

cases.title: ACL Applied to Wrong Interface or Direction

scenario.symptom: A network service works from one direction but fails when traffic enters or leaves a particular interface.

observations.description: The ACL is applied to the wrong interface or in the wrong direction.

next_command.reason: Determine which ACL is applied to which interface and in which direction.

expected_evidence.interpretation: The ACL is applied outbound even though the intended policy requires inbound filtering.

diagnosis.explanation: The ACL is attached to an incorrect interface or applied in the wrong direction relative to the intended security policy.

recommended_fix.description: Apply the ACL to the intended interface and direction according to the network security policy.

verification.expected_result: The ACL is applied at the intended enforcement point and traffic follows the expected security policy.

cases.title: ACL Rule Order Causes Unexpected Denial

scenario.symptom: HTTPS traffic should be permitted, but the connection is denied even though a permit rule exists.

expected_state.policy: HTTPS traffic to Server-01 should be permitted.

observations.description: The HTTPS connection to Server-01 fails.

next_command.reason: Inspect ACL entries in evaluation order and determine which rule matches the HTTPS traffic first.

expected_evidence.interpretation: A broad deny rule appears before the specific HTTPS permit rule.
The HTTPS permit rule exists but is evaluated after the broader deny rule.

diagnosis.explanation: ACL entries are evaluated from top to bottom, so the broad deny rule matches before the specific HTTPS permit rule.

recommended_fix.description: Reorder or modify the ACL entries according to the intended security policy.

verification.expected_result: HTTPS traffic matches the intended permit rule while unrelated traffic remains subject to the intended restrictions.

scenario.symptom: A client connection appears to leave successfully, but the application session does not establish because return traffic is blocked.

expected_state.policy: Legitimate return traffic must be permitted.

observations.description: The client initiates a connection but the application session does not establish.

next_command.reason: Determine whether ACL counters or deny entries indicate that required return traffic is being blocked.

expected_evidence.interpretation: The ACL contains a deny condition matching traffic on the return path.

diagnosis.explanation: The forward path is available, but the ACL blocks traffic required to complete the return path of the connection.

recommended_fix.description: Adjust the ACL according to the intended security policy so that legitimate return traffic is permitted.

verification.expected_result: The required return traffic is permitted and the end-to-end application session establishes successfully.

scenario.symptom: Internal clients can reach the router but cannot access an external network.

observations.description: The client can reach its local gateway but cannot reach the external network.

next_command.reason: Determine whether traffic from the inside network is being translated.

expected_evidence.interpretation: No active NAT translation exists for the internal client traffic.

diagnosis.explanation: The internal client traffic is not producing a NAT translation, so the external network cannot receive traffic using the expected translated address.

recommended_fix.description: Verify and configure the appropriate NAT policy for the inside network according to the intended topology.

verification.expected_result: A NAT translation is created when the internal client initiates external traffic and the connection succeeds.

cases.title: Incorrect NAT Inside or Outside Interface

scenario.symptom: NAT configuration exists, but internal traffic is not translated correctly.

observations.description: The client cannot establish external connectivity even though NAT rules are configured.

next_command.reason: Inspect which router interfaces are configured as NAT inside and NAT outside.

expected_evidence.interpretation: The LAN-facing interface has been incorrectly configured as NAT outside/inside.

diagnosis.explanation: The NAT inside/outside roles do not match the intended LAN-to-WAN topology.

recommended_fix.description: Correct the NAT inside and outside interface roles according to the intended topology.

verification.expected_result: The LAN interface is configured as NAT inside, the WAN interface as NAT outside, and translations are created for external traffic.

scenario.symptom: PC-01 can reach an IP address but cannot access the same service using its hostname.

observations.description: Hostname resolution fails while direct IP connectivity works.

next_command.reason: Verify which DNS server address is configured on the client.

expected_evidence.interpretation: The client is configured to use the wrong DNS server.

diagnosis.explanation: PC-01 is configured with a DNS server address that does not match the intended network service.

recommended_fix.description: Configure the correct DNS server address on PC-01 or through the appropriate DHCP configuration.

verification.expected_result: PC-01 uses the intended DNS server and can resolve the required hostname.

scenario.symptom: Clients can reach the DNS server but a specific hostname does not resolve to the expected IP address.

observations.description: server01.lab.local does not resolve to the expected address.

next_command.reason: Determine whether DNS returns an address and whether the returned address matches the intended server.

expected_evidence.interpretation: The DNS server does not have a matching record for the requested hostname.

diagnosis.explanation: The requested hostname does not have the expected DNS record.

recommended_fix.description: Create or correct the DNS record so that the hostname resolves to the intended IP address.

verification.expected_result: nslookup returns 192.168.30.50 for server01.lab.local.

cases.title: Incorrect Wireless SSID or Authentication Configuration

scenario.symptom: A wireless client cannot connect to the expected network.

observations.description: The client cannot successfully associate with the expected wireless network.

next_command.reason: Inspect the wireless network configuration and compare the SSID and authentication settings with the intended lab configuration.

expected_evidence.interpretation: Verify that the expected SSID exists and inspect its associated authentication configuration.

diagnosis.explanation: The wireless client and access point configuration do not match the intended SSID or authentication settings.

recommended_fix.description: Correct the SSID and authentication configuration so the client and access point use the intended wireless settings.

verification.expected_result: The client successfully associates with the intended SSID and receives normal network connectivity.

cases.title: Wireless Client Connected but No Network Connectivity

scenario.symptom: A wireless client successfully associates with the access point but cannot reach network resources.

observations.description: The client is associated with the wireless network but cannot reach its gateway or network resources.

next_command.reason: Verify that the VLAN used by the wireless network exists and that the access point's switch port is correctly assigned.

expected_evidence.interpretation: The VLAN expected by the wireless network is missing from the switch.

diagnosis.explanation: The wireless client is associated successfully, but the network VLAN required to carry its traffic is not available on the switch.

recommended_fix.description: Create or restore the required wireless VLAN and configure the access point uplink according to the intended topology.

verification.expected_result: The wireless VLAN is available, the client receives the expected network configuration, and it can reach its gateway.
